name: Negative Approach
label: Touch and Go
lede: Four Detroit teenagers, one ten-song seven-inch, one sixteen-minute album, and a singer whose scream still makes grown punks step back from the stage.

eras.title: Skate park kids on a Touch and Go sampler
eras.text: John Brannon had grown up on Creem magazine, the Stooges and the MC5, and in the summer of 1981 hardcore gave him a way in. He built Negative Approach out of teenagers he met at Detroit skate parks, and within months the band was on the first Touch and Go record and playing the East Coast.

years.h: John Brannon and Pete Zelewski start Negative Approach
years.p: John Brannon and bassist Pete Zelewski form Negative Approach in Detroit after seeing [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] play, according to a 2023 CBS News profile of the band.

years.h: The McCulloch brothers and Opie Moore lock in
years.p: Pete Zelewski leaves early. John Brannon settles on [[Rob McCulloch|0071a9c5-d23d-4117-a9d1-656cddcf2fd1]] on guitar, his brother [[Graham McCulloch|a9cb94ec-b297-44d5-9ea1-dbefe4b26c33]] on bass and Chris "Opie" Moore on drums, most of them 15 or 16 years old.
years.xp: John Brannon told Vice that the band's age was its biggest limit: kids that young couldn't just get in a van and tour. Metro Times says Brannon recruited the players from local skateboard parks and built an all-ages scene of underground shows for kids like them.

years.h: Lost Cause opens Touch and Go's Process of Elimination EP
years.p: Negative Approach's first release is the song Lost Cause on Process of Elimination, a Touch and Go 7" sampler of Midwest hardcore. A three-show tour of Boston, New York and Washington, D.C. follows.

years.h: John Brannon in the slam pit when Fear plays Saturday Night Live
years.p: John Belushi brings a crew of hardcore kids to NBC for [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]]'s Halloween 1981 performance. Metro Times says Belushi gave John Brannon his mohawk and Brannon grabbed a microphone on live TV.
years.xp: Brannon was roadying for the [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] at the time, according to Vice. [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]] of [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] was in the same slam pit. The broadcast went down as one of the most chaotic nights in the show's history.

eras.title: Ten songs, one seven-inch
eras.text: Negative Approach's debut crammed ten songs onto one small record, none of them long enough to catch your breath. The live show was worse, or better: John Brannon treated every gig as the band against the room.

years.src: Wikipedia: Negative Approach (EP) · Metro Times (2010) · Austin Chronicle (2006)
years.h: Negative Approach EP · Touch and Go
years.p: Recorded in April 1982 with [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] producing, the Negative Approach EP fits ten songs on one 7". Pressure lasts nine seconds; the longest track runs under two minutes.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the first pressing was 3,000 copies. The cover borrowed its imagery from The Exorcist, according to Metro Times. The Austin Chronicle credits Larissa Strickland, later of [[Laughing Hyenas|a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e]], with booking the band's early shows and co-writing Lead Song on the record.

Metro Times quotes a fellow musician calling it the greatest hardcore EP ever; the record has been bootlegged and reissued ever since.

yt: Negative Approach live at the Freezer Theater, 1982
years.h: Negative Approach, Minor Threat and a riot at the Freezer Theater
years.p: Negative Approach opens for [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] at the Freezer Theater on Cass Avenue. Metro Times says a riot broke out in the parking lot, windows were smashed, people were arrested and the Freezer never reopened.
years.xp: Metro Times' 2010 account puts [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] on the same bill; its 2016 story calls it the Freezer's final show. The Minor Threat date comes from the band's show archive.

q: Me and the band against the audience.
years.h: John Brannon's live rule: Negative Approach versus the crowd
years.p: John Brannon ran Negative Approach shows as a confrontation, and fights in the crowd became part of the draw.

eras.title: Tied Down, then torn apart
eras.text: Negative Approach made its only album in the summer of 1983 and fell apart before anyone could buy it. The crowds had grown, the fights had grown with them, and the band's drummer wanted out.

years.h: Tied Down, Negative Approach's only album · Touch and Go
years.p: Ten songs in 16 minutes 53 seconds, recorded in August 1983 at Multi Track Studios in Redford, Michigan, with Corey Rusk producing and Lloyd Grace engineering.
years.xp: The line-up was John Brannon, Rob McCulloch on guitar, Graham McCulloch on bass and Chris "OP" Moore on drums. Corey Rusk also shot the photos for the lyric sheet. Metro Times says the band had already split by the time the record came out.

q: I was getting sick of the fact that it started getting popular.
years.h: Negative Approach splits a week before Texas shows with Big Boys
years.p: The original Negative Approach falls apart on the road, a week before planned Texas dates with [[Big Boys|fde1cff2-5a7b-4e8c-9666-110fa90500fb]], according to the Austin Chronicle. Opie Moore was tired of the growing crowds and the fights.
years.xp: John Brannon later told Metro Times that hardcore had simply run its course for him. Members wanted to take the music somewhere else, and some fans were showing up for the violence, not the songs.

years.h: John Brannon's new Negative Approach line-up dies fast
years.p: John Brannon puts together an entirely new Negative Approach after Tied Down. CBS News says it dissolved after a handful of dates in 1984.

years.h: Graham McCulloch joins The Meatmen in Washington, D.C.
years.p: Bassist Graham McCulloch moves on to [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]]'s [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]], now based in D.C. with ex-[[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] guitarists [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] and [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]]. He plays with them until 1988.

years.h: John Brannon and Larissa Strickland form Laughing Hyenas
years.p: In Ann Arbor, John Brannon starts [[Laughing Hyenas|a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e]] with guitarist Larissa Strickland. Their first show is in April 1985, and the band runs until 1995.

eras.title: A bootleg legend grows
eras.text: With Negative Approach gone, its two records became passwords among hardcore fans. John Brannon spent twenty years screaming for other bands while the McCulloch brothers and Opie Moore moved on.

years.h: Touch and Go collects Negative Approach on Total Recall
years.p: Total Recall puts the EP and Tied Down on one release for a generation that had only heard the band on tape.
years.xp: By then the members were scattered. Opie Moore and Rob McCulloch played together in the alt-rock band Crossed Wire; Graham McCulloch had gone from The Meatmen to Earth 18 with Void's Bubba Dupree, then Mother May I. Moore later went solo as a roots singer-songwriter.

years.h: John Brannon fronts Easy Action
years.p: After Laughing Hyenas end in 1995, John Brannon starts the Detroit rock band Easy Action, home of guitarist [[Harold Richardson|b6e5c3cb-d902-4c81-ad4e-9c2c6e546826]] and bassist [[Ron Sakowski|0a176fe9-0c15-44a6-a227-ef345f441acb]]. Their debut album comes out on Reptilian in 2001.

years.h: Ready to Fight digs up Negative Approach demos and live tapes
years.p: Reptilian releases Ready to Fight: Demos, Live and Unreleased 1981–83, the first new Negative Approach material in more than twenty years.

eras.title: Twenty-three years later
eras.text: Corey Rusk asked, and John Brannon said yes to something he never expected to do. The reunion band was half original, half Easy Action, and it sounded as mean as 1983.

years.src: Metro Times (2010) · Austin Chronicle (2006) · CBS News (2023)
years.h: Negative Approach reforms without the McCulloch brothers
years.p: John Brannon and Opie Moore reunite for Touch and Go's 25th anniversary with Easy Action's Harold Richardson on guitar and Ron Sakowski on bass. Metro Times says they practiced twice, in Richardson's basement.
years.xp:
Brannon told the Austin Chronicle he had lost touch with Rob and Graham McCulloch. When he called one of them about the reunion, he said, the conversation had turned to insults by the second call.

Sakowski had played bass in Laughing Hyenas and Easy Action; CBS News also lists him as a former [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] bassist.

years.h: First Negative Approach show since 1983, at Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: Negative Approach returns at Touch and Go's anniversary weekend in Chicago, on a bill with the label's other reunited bands, including [[Killdozer|6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38]]. Metro Times says the outdoor show drew about 7,000 people.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas · CelebrityAccess · Austin Chronicle (2006)
years.h: Larissa Strickland dies at 46
years.p: Laughing Hyenas guitarist Larissa Strickland, John Brannon's former partner, dies in North Port, Florida. CelebrityAccess reported an apparent overdose of the prescription drug Xanax.
years.xp: The Austin Chronicle wrote that Strickland booked Negative Approach's early shows, co-wrote a song on their first record and shaped the band.

years.h: Negative Approach plays London and All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: A London show on December 7 and All Tomorrow's Parties on December 10, on a bill with [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]] and the [[MC5|08b736bb-1c82-40b4-8b0b-49e2182a067a]], the Detroit bands John Brannon grew up on.

years.h: Negative Approach backs Tesco Vee in Detroit
years.p: Negative Approach serves as [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] frontman [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]]'s backing band for a 30-minute set in Detroit. Tesco Vee says it got him performing again.

years.h: Negative Approach tours the Northeast and Europe
years.p: An April run through the Northeast and a June tour of Europe. Brannon later told Vice the band had been to Europe five times since the reunion.

years.h: Negative Approach plays Tony Rettman's Detroit hardcore book party
years.p: At St. Andrew's Hall in Detroit, Negative Approach celebrates Tony Rettman's book Why Be Something That You're Not, named after one of their songs, a history of Detroit hardcore.

years.h: Nothing Will Stand in Our Way · Taang! Records
years.p: Taang! releases unreleased Negative Approach recordings from 1984, the short-lived second line-up. The band plays Fun Fun Fun Fest in Austin the same month.

eras.title: Still no email
eras.text: The reunion was supposed to be one show. A decade on, Negative Approach was headlining clubs and German metal festivals, and John Brannon still didn't own a computer.

years.h: John Brannon tells Vice he never planned a reunion
years.p: John Brannon says he never expected to put Negative Approach back together, has no computer or email, and does it for the fight, not the money.

years.h: Negative Approach at Third Man Records, and talk of new songs
years.p: After a show at Jack White's Third Man Records in Detroit, John Brannon tells Metro Times it's time for new Negative Approach songs, with Opie Moore coming in from Brooklyn. Wacken Open Air is booked for summer.

years.h: Dope, Hookers and Pavement tells Detroit hardcore's story
years.p: The documentary on Detroit hardcore, with members of Negative Approach, [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] and [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], comes out during the pandemic.

years.h: Negative Approach on the road with OFF! and Circle Jerks
years.p: Back after the pandemic, Negative Approach tours with [[OFF!|da9a1492-47c2-4e93-8b2b-04555be23efb]], Punch and [[Circle Jerks|22995eba-1238-4b4f-a937-ac2c5767ab9f]], with John Brannon still out front.
